newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends down, meal mixed as soybeans fade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends down, meal mixed as soybeans fade.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed lower and soymeal values ended mixed on a retracement in the soybean pit, traders said.
News of ample rains over the weekend in Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul overwhelmed the market with talk the moisture will improve what were expected to be bumper crops.
But soybean traders shrugged off the bearish weather factor and rallied at midsession, dragging soy products higher and lending support to corn and wheat futures, traders said.
"One rain doesn't make a crop," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter, noting it was still early in the growing season.

Traders also noted talk that a private analytical firm had trimmed its U.S. soybean ending stocks projection to 137 million tonnes from 140 million. USDA pegged stocks at 155 million tonnes, or about 20 days' supply.

Funds were strong buyers of both soyoil and soymeal, accounting for at least 1,100 lots of soymeal and 1,200 lots of soyoil. Traders said Cargill Investor Services and E.D. and F. Man International were buyers of the March soymeal.
Soymeal closed $0.90 per ton higher to $0.40 lower with March unchanged at $236.70 a ton. Soyoil closed 0.05 to 0.13 per lb lower with March down 0.11 at 24.33 cents.
Commercials were on both sides of the soymeal market and ADM reportedly sold at least 1,200 lots of soyoil on the day. Cargill was also a strong seller of March soyoil.
Soymeal volume was estimated at 32,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 25,979 lots. Soyoil volume was estimated at 27,000 lots, against Friday's tally of 20,941.
